info.title: Power Pet Door
info.description:
The wire protocol a High Tech Pet Power Pet Door speaks on TCP 3000. Reverse-engineered, and generated by exercising the simulator - so every message shape here is one the simulator actually produced.

This describes the *shapes*. What a real door does with them - the commands it accepts and silently ignores, the values it saturates rather than refuses, why door motion uses a different envelope key - is in docs/protocol.md, and no schema has anywhere to put it.

Commands the door accepts but cannot act on are deliberately absent - see docs/protocol.md for those; sending one is never correct.

SET_SCHEDULE.summary: Sent under the `config` envelope key. Verified to take effect - `GET_SCHEDULE` reflects it.
SET_SCHEDULE.description: Create or replace one schedule slot. The slot number goes beside the schedule object, not only inside it.

externalDocs.description: What a real door does with this

config.description: Names the command. Door motion uses `cmd`; everything else uses `config`.

msgId.description: Correlation token, echoed back as `msgID` - note the capital D. Any value will do; match the reply back to the request that used it.

dir.description: Phone to door. Optional - the door answers a request without it - but every client observed sends it, and it is the counterpart of the `d2p` on every reply.

index.description: Schedule slot. `SET_SCHEDULE` needs it as a **sibling** of `schedule`, even though the schedule object carries one too.

schedule.description: One schedule. Times are `{"hour": h, "min": m}`; a window ending at its start is empty, not all-day.

index.description: Which slot this schedule occupies. `SET_SCHEDULE` needs it here **and** as a sibling of `schedule`.

enabled.description: Whether this slot is in force. An int here, not a string.

daysOfWeek.description: Seven flags, **Sunday first**, `1` for a day the schedule applies. A legacy integer bitmask with bit 0 = Sunday is also accepted on input.

inside.description: Whether this schedule governs the **indoor** sensor. Note this is not the `settings` flag of the same name.

outside.description: Whether this schedule governs the **outdoor** sensor. Note this is not the `settings` flag of the same name.

hour.description: Hour, 24-hour clock, in the door's own timezone. **24 is legal and means the end of the day** - a window of `20:00-24:00` reports the sensor enabled at 21:07. Hour 24 is only a time when the minute is `0`.

min.description: Minute past the hour. Must be `0` when the hour is 24.

SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE.name: SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE
SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE.title: SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE
SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE.summary: Sent under the `config` envelope key. Verified to take effect - `GET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE` reflects it.
SET_SENSOR_TRIGGER_VOLTAGE.description: Set how strong a collar signal must be to count as a pet. Raising it makes the door less eager; lowering it catches a weak collar.

externalDocs.description: What a real door does with this

config.description: Names the command. Door motion uses `cmd`; everything else uses `config`.

msgId.description: Correlation token, echoed back as `msgID` - note the capital D. Any value will do; match the reply back to the request that used it.

dir.description: Phone to door. Optional - the door answers a request without it - but every client observed sends it, and it is the counterpart of the `d2p` on every reply.

voltage.description: Collar detection threshold; a typical unit ships at 2000. Stored as a signed 32-bit value, so larger numbers saturate at the maximum. A value of 0 is answered with success and leaves the stored value unchanged, so read it back to confirm. The reply reports it as `sensorTriggerVoltage`. In millivolts.
